name: archally-blueprint-navigation
description: Go-to-definition, hover, highlight, and re-index for Archally blueprint IDs (e.g. slice.TYPE### references) across .blueprint YAML files.

archallyBlueprint.fileGlob.description: Glob for the blueprint YAML files to index for id navigation.

archallyBlueprint.highlight.enabled.description: Highlight blueprint IDs (slice.TYPE###, bare TYPE###, MIG###, CAT####) with a distinct color/style.

archallyBlueprint.highlight.color.description: Override color for highlighted IDs (any CSS color, e.g. #c586c0). Empty = use the themed 'archallyBlueprint.idForeground' color (override that via workbench.colorCustomizations).

archallyBlueprint.highlight.fontStyle.description: Font style for highlighted IDs. Note: the editor font FAMILY cannot be changed per token — only weight/style/underline.

archallyBlueprint.codeRef.enabled.description: Turn code_ref paths in .blueprint YAML into clickable links that open the file on the configured git host (from `repository`/`repositories` in blueprint.yaml). Local-clone resolution is added in a later release.

archallyBlueprint.codeRef.highlight.enab.description: Color code_ref paths (distinct from blueprint IDs) to mark them as clickable source links.

archallyBlueprint.codeRef.highlight.colo.description: Override color for highlighted code_ref paths (any CSS color, e.g. #4daafc). Empty = use the themed 'archallyBlueprint.codeRefForeground' color.

archallyBlueprint.codeRef.highlight.font.description: Font style for highlighted code_ref paths. Default underline (a link affordance).

archallyBlueprint.referenceLinks.enabled.description: Linkify http(s) URLs anywhere in .blueprint YAML (evidence sources, trackers, docs) → open in the browser, and evidence[].source file-paths → open the local workspace file. Shares the code_ref link colour.

colors.description: Foreground color used to highlight known Archally blueprint IDs. Default: canary yellow.
Foreground color for clickable code_ref paths (distinct from blueprint IDs). Default: link blue.
